grade.notes: The plan is solid and specific, but the first day stacks a 15-minute coordination step on the 5-minute setup step, and the first real step depends on teammates agreeing on a time, which is out of the student's control. Some steps carry hidden decisions (e.g. which shop, which roles), and the plan treats steps 13 and 14 as conditional without checking the requirements first.

plan.taskTitle: Build a marketing plan for a local coffee shop with your 3 teammates
plan.analysis: Start with a tiny setup action, then pace group coordination, research, drafting and review in a few sessions per week so everything is finished a day before Oct 20.

steps.title: Create the shared doc and invite teammates
steps.description: Create a Google Doc named 'Coffee Shop Marketing Plan', paste in the assignment prompt and deadline (Oct 20), and share the link in your group chat. Done when the link is sent.

steps.title: Propose a kickoff meeting and split roles
steps.description: In the group chat, suggest 2 meeting times this week and propose four roles: market research, branding and messaging, channels and budget, and editing and slides. Done when a time is agreed on.

steps.title: Hold kickoff meeting and assign sections
steps.description: Meet for 45 minutes to pick the coffee shop, confirm the required plan sections from the prompt, assign each person a section, and set internal deadlines. Write the assignments at the top of the doc.

steps.title: Visit or research the coffee shop
steps.description: Visit the shop or study its website, Instagram and Google reviews, noting 5 facts about its menu, prices, location, customers and current marketing. Paste the notes into the doc under 'Shop Overview'.

steps.title: Research your section's competitors and audience
steps.description: For your assigned section, look at 3 nearby competing cafes and find data on local customers. Write bullet-point findings in the doc with links to your sources.

steps.title: Draft SWOT and target audience
steps.description: As a group, or split up if needed, write a SWOT analysis and 2 customer personas using the shop overview and competitor notes. Done when both sit in the doc in rough form.

steps.title: Group check-in on goals and strategy
steps.description: Meet for 30 minutes to agree on 3 measurable marketing goals and the core positioning, and to fix any gaps in the research. Note the decisions in the doc.

steps.title: Draft your section of the plan
steps.description: Write a full first draft of your assigned section (for example branding, social media, promotions or budget) in about 500 words. Done when it is in the doc, even if rough.

steps.title: Continue drafting and build the budget
steps.description: Finish your draft section, and have the channels person build a simple budget table and a 3-month timeline of campaigns. Done when every section has a complete draft.

steps.title: Peer review teammates' sections
steps.description: Read two teammates' sections and leave comments on clarity, consistency with the goals, and missing details. Done when you have left at least 3 comments on each.

steps.title: Revise your section from feedback
steps.description: Go through the comments on your section and revise it, resolving each one. Done when all comments are resolved or answered.

steps.title: Write the executive summary and assemble the plan
steps.description: The editor combines the sections, writes a one-page executive summary, and unifies formatting and headings. Others fix any overlaps flagged in the doc.

steps.title: Build slides or presentation materials if required
steps.description: Turn the main points into 8-10 slides with one key idea each, and split the speaking parts. Skip if only a written plan is due and use the time for polishing.

steps.title: Final group review and proofread
steps.description: Meet for 60 minutes to read the full plan aloud, fix typos, check sources and the budget numbers, and rehearse if presenting. Done when everyone approves the final version.

steps.title: Submit the final plan
steps.description: Export to PDF, check that all four names are on it, and submit it as required. Confirm the submission in the group chat.

grade.notes: The plan says 8 sessions, but only 2 sprints plus 6 sessions are scheduled, and the sessions are not actually tied to the computed page ranges (session numbering is inconsistent, e.g. 'session 4' follows the listen session). The schedule also has odd gaps (Sat, Mon, then Oct 7) and the first step bundles a pen and bookmark setup, but otherwise it is engaging.

plan.taskTitle: Finish reading Sapiens
plan.analysis: With no deadline, pace the remaining reading in short timeboxed sessions over about two weeks, varying the activity each time with small hooks to keep it from feeling dull.

steps.title: Set up your reading spot
steps.description: Put your copy of Sapiens on your pillow or desk, and open to your bookmark (or stick a sticky note on the page where you stopped). Done when the book is open and a pen is resting on it.

steps.title: 20-minute sprint: read and mark one surprise
steps.description: Set a 20-minute timer and read from your bookmark without stopping. Hook: underline or flag the single most surprising claim you find, and stop when the timer ends.

steps.title: Count remaining pages and split them
steps.description: Check how many pages are left, divide by 8 sessions, and write the page target on a sticky note inside the cover. Done when each upcoming session has a page range.

steps.title: Read session 1 on your feet or somewhere new
steps.description: Set a 40-minute timer and read your first page range somewhere different, like a cafe, library or the couch. Challenge: beat your page target before the timer ends.

steps.title: Read session 2 with a 1-line recap
steps.description: Set a 40-minute timer and read your next page range. Afterward, write a one-sentence summary of what you read in the margin or your phone notes.

steps.title: Listen-and-read session
steps.description: Play an audiobook or a YouTube talk by Yuval Noah Harari on the section you're reading for 15 minutes, then read the matching pages for 25 minutes. Done when you've covered your next page range.

steps.title: Read session 4 and rate the chapter
steps.description: Set a 40-minute timer and read your next page range. When done, give the chapter a score out of 10 and jot down one reason why.

steps.title: Read session 5 with a debate question
steps.description: Set a 35-minute timer and read the next range while looking for one claim you disagree with. Write a one-line counterargument in the margin.

steps.title: Read session 6 in a 2-part split
steps.description: Read for 20 minutes, take a 5-minute walk or stretch, then read 20 more minutes. Done when you've reached the end of your page range.

steps.title: Final push to the last page
steps.description: Set a 40-minute timer and read the remaining pages through the book's final chapter. Done when you've closed the book after the last page.

steps.title: Write your 3-line takeaway
steps.description: Spend 5 minutes writing three lines on your phone or a sticky note: the biggest idea, the most surprising fact, and whether you'd recommend Sapiens. Done when it's saved and the book is back on your shelf.

grade.notes: Step 1 is tiny, but step 2 (20 min account creation) also lands on day one, and the FSA ID can take time to verify. Step 4, asking the parent, comes after gathering docs and is placed late; it should come earlier since avoiders may delay it and the parent also needs their own FSA ID. The Oct 7 to Oct 9 gap after Sunday Oct 4 is loose, and the plan never acknowledges that the 'Just...' phrasing could feel repetitive.

plan.taskTitle: Submit the FAFSA for the next school year
plan.analysis: Break the FAFSA into tiny, low-pressure sessions spread across the 10 days: gather documents, create the login, fill it in by section, then review and submit a couple of days early.

steps.title: Open the FAFSA site and leave it in a tab
steps.description: Just type studentaid.gov into your browser and leave the page open in a tab. That's it, nothing to fill in yet.

steps.title: Make a FSA ID (or find your existing one)
steps.description: Just click 'Create Account' and follow the prompts with your email and phone. If you already have one, just log in to confirm it works. Done when you're logged in.

steps.title: Gather your documents in one folder
steps.description: Just pull up your Social Security number, driver's license, and a photo or PDF of last year's tax return or W-2s. Put them in one folder on your desktop. Done when the folder exists, even if a few items are missing.

steps.title: Ask a parent for their part (if you're dependent)
steps.description: Just send one short text or email: 'Can we spend 30 min on the FAFSA this weekend? I need your FSA ID and tax info.' Done when the message is sent.

steps.title: Fill in your personal info and school list
steps.description: Just start the form and complete the sections about you, plus add the schools you want to receive your FAFSA. Save and stop when those sections are done.

steps.title: Complete the parent and financial sections together
steps.description: Just sit down with your parent and work through the tax and income sections, using the IRS data link if it's offered. Done when every required section shows complete.

steps.title: Do a gentle review pass
steps.description: Just read through the summary page once, checking names, SSN, and school codes for typos. Done when you've fixed anything off or confirmed it looks right.

steps.title: Sign and submit
steps.description: Just have you and your parent e-sign with your FSA IDs, then click Submit. Done when you see the confirmation page.

steps.title: Save your confirmation
steps.description: Just screenshot or download the confirmation and drop it in your FAFSA folder. Then you can celebrate.

steps.title: Check for follow-up requests
steps.description: Just check your email and each school's portal for any missing items. Done when you've either found nothing or noted what to send.

grade.notes: Step 3 (45 min skimming two primary texts) is too big and vague for an avoider, and steps 5-8 pack a lot of writing into Thursday with no buffer. The repeated "Just..." phrasing also gets formulaic, though the low-pressure tone and the 5-minute first step suit an avoider.

plan.taskTitle: Write a 3-page essay comparing Plato and Aristotle on justice
plan.analysis: With only today and tomorrow, we'll split the essay into small, low-pressure sessions: set up, a bit of gathering, a simple plan, then drafting in two chunks today and tomorrow, and finally a gentle polish.

steps.title: Open your doc and paste in the prompt
steps.description: Just open a new doc called 'Plato vs Aristotle – Justice' and paste in the assignment prompt. That's it, and you're allowed to stop after this if you want.

steps.title: Jot down what you already know
steps.description: Just type a few messy bullets under 'Plato' and 'Aristotle' for whatever you remember about justice, like the Republic's harmony of the soul and Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics Book V. Stop when you have 3-4 bullets each; they can be rough.

steps.title: Skim your sources for key points
steps.description: Just skim Republic Book IV (justice as each part doing its own work) and Nicomachean Ethics Book V (distributive and corrective justice). Copy down one or two quotes for each thinker with page numbers.

steps.title: Sketch a simple 5-line outline
steps.description: Just write one line each for: intro with thesis, Plato's view, Aristotle's view, key differences, and conclusion. A thesis like 'Plato sees justice as inner and structural, Aristotle as practical and relational' is plenty.

steps.title: Draft the intro and Plato section
steps.description: Just write the intro and the Plato paragraphs, about 1.5 pages, and don't worry about polish. Done means the words exist on the page.

steps.title: Draft the Aristotle section
steps.description: Just write the Aristotle paragraphs, about 1 page, using your quotes on distributive and corrective justice. Rough is fine.

steps.title: Write the comparison and conclusion
steps.description: Just write the paragraph on how they differ (inner harmony vs. fair treatment between people) and a short conclusion that restates your thesis. Done means you have a full rough draft at about 3 pages.

steps.title: Read through, tidy up, and submit
steps.description: Just read it once aloud, fix awkward sentences, check your quotes and citations, and submit. Good enough is the goal.

grade.notes: First step is concrete but slightly bundles tasks (create file, paste prompt, copy first problem) and could be tinier. Step 7 has a minor wording glitch ("office hours and office email"), and there's no buffer for Tuesday, and the flagged-problem fix is saved for Monday with little slack.

plan.taskTitle: Finish 20 hypothesis testing problems in R
plan.analysis: Get the setup done immediately, then knock out the problems in four small batches spread across the week, leaving a review session before the Tuesday deadline.

steps.title: Set up your R script
steps.description: Open RStudio, create a new script called 'hw_hypothesis_testing.R', and paste in the assignment prompt as comments at the top. Done when the file is saved and the first problem is copied below it.

steps.title: Review the test functions you'll need
steps.description: Skim your lecture notes or textbook section and write a comment cheat sheet in your script for t.test(), prop.test(), chisq.test(), and var.test(), plus when to use each. Done when you have one example line for each function.

steps.title: Solve problems 1-5
steps.description: For each problem, state H0 and Ha in comments, run the appropriate test in R, and write your conclusion in one sentence. Done when problems 1-5 have code, output, and a written conclusion.

steps.title: Solve problems 6-10
steps.description: Use the same routine: hypotheses, R test, interpretation with the p-value and your alpha level. Done when problems 6-10 are finished and the script runs without errors.

steps.title: Solve problems 11-15
steps.description: Work through the next five using the same routine, and flag any problem you're unsure about with a '# CHECK' comment. Done when all five have answers and flagged items are marked.

steps.title: Solve problems 16-20
steps.description: Finish the last five problems with hypotheses, code, and conclusions. Done when every problem has an answer in your script.

steps.title: Fix flagged problems and review
steps.description: Resolve each '# CHECK' item using your notes or office hours and office email if needed, then re-run the whole script from top to bottom to confirm no errors. Done when every conclusion matches its output.

steps.title: Format and submit
steps.description: Knit or export your script and output into the format your instructor requires, check that all 20 problems appear, and upload it. Done when you see the submission confirmation.
